utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then we may regard the appeal as ripe for hearing, and notwithstanding that we are all still robed, we will proceed immediately to regard ourselves as sitting in a Status Conference to consider matters pertinent to the holding of a hearing on the merits of the appeal. I would suggest that there are two branches of the matter to be considered: (1) the likely duration of the appeal hearing; (2) the number of rounds to be allocated to each side; (3) the duration of each round; and (4) I think there is another point about establishing the time period in the calendar for the holding of the hearing. So I have passed beyond my initial mention of two points. I think I have covered four points. Would counsel for the appellant like to speak first?

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: I would think that one week would be more than sufficient to be able to dispose of the appeal. It may well be that one wouldn't require a fifth day, but I think, to be on the safe side, if a week were set aside, it would be very comfortable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: We understand that some of you gentlemen may have commitments, and I hasten to emphasise, in case there is any doubt, that to the extent possible, the Court would be glad to take account of any commitments counsel at the bar may have. There should be no question of that. On the other hand, I do hope that counsel will appreciate that the time constraints on the Court are enormous. Now, we had in mind the week beginning 19th of April. How does that respond to your situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: That would be a week that would be convenient for me professionally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Convenient to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: What about the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As far as I know, Your Honour, I would be the only one who might have a conflict with a trial, but certainly my other colleagues would be more than able to carry on if I do have a trial that week, but right now we have no firm schedule in that case, so as far as we know, the dates are fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: May I assume that you, not being in a position to urge anything to the contrary, find the suggestion acceptable?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: We will hold the hearing during the week commencing the 19th of April. What about the configuration of the hearing? Should there be two rounds, three rounds, four rounds?

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: I would have suggested tentatively that the appeal would perhaps best be heard, as it were, in two parts, and that the appellant's appeal should be heard first, responded to, and then with me having the right of reply; and then beginning again with the respondent's appeal, my submissions, and then a right of reply for the respondent. So tentatively, I would suggest if we keep the submissions in two discrete parts, it will avoid confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I see that. That's very attractive, Mr. Clegg. Do you think that there is a risk of duplication in that methodology?

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: Not if we do it that way, I don't think there are. I don't think there is any risk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Counsel will bear in mind things which have been said previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: We will bear in mind that the Court only needs to hear something once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: The Prosecution nods in agreement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We were going to suggest the same thing. Of course, there would be three parts, the appeal on sentencing being the last part. So we could deal with the appellant's appeal, the cross appeal, and then sentencing as the final matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Why don't we try to combine it this way: We hold one hearing in relation to the appellant's appeal from conviction and the Prosecution appeal from conviction; is that right? Partly from?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Let me make sure that I'm not confused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: So I understand --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Deal with the appellant's appeal in the first instance, their submissions, then our submissions -- our response to their appeal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: So we will hear those two appeals together?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not our appeal, just our response to their appeal issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then you will have to have three appeals, three hearings.

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Well, three segments. We believe they can all be dealt with in the same hearing, that is, the same set of days that are structured, but for logical purposes, we think that to deal with the appellant's submissions, our response to that, then, second, deal with our appeals issues as to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: What does the note-taker write on his record? Which case does he write on his record?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: It would be the same case and the briefs are labelled as appellant's notice of appeal, we are cross appellant, and it could be referred to that way. So we would deal with appellant's notice of appeal and our response to that, similar to what we're dealing with today; then we would deal with the cross appellant's notice --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then, finally, the sentence appeal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Then, finally, the sentencing appeal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: The document kept by the recorder would state each appeal separately at different stages; is that your vision of it, Mr. Clegg?

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: We accept that format in principle. I imagine we will all recognise a need to refine it as we come to the batting crease; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. One point, if I may, so that we can be sure: Is it now the case, based on the ruling today, that the sole grounds of appeal by the appellant are grounds 1 and 3 as stated in the amended notice? That's all we're addressing now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: That is what is meant by supersession, which I think was the root word used by the appellant in the chapeau of his amended notice of appeal; is that right, Mr. Clegg?

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: That what went before goes through the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I just want to make sure there's been some practice here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: That helps you with your problems about alleged defects?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: The window has had a fair bit thrown through it already, but we were hoping to add to that. There was originally drafted an appellant's response to the respondent's appeal; in other words, it was what the appellant was saying in relation to their appeal against his acquittal in relation to a number of charges. Again, I have refined, produced a new document, which I know has been filed, and we would seek to substitute that in preference to the rather longer document that superseded it. I don't know if Mr. Keegan has any objection to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have filed, of course, an objection to the submission of a new pleading at this point again on the same basis, and we are not in a position to say whether that, in keeping with your decision of today, could merely be supplanted for the prior submission, because, again, without having an opportunity to look at the substance, we don't know if we would, in fact, desire the right to respond as is normally given. The time for filing of appeal brief has long run, and absent a showing of the necessity, we don't believe it should be accepted at this late stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: On that matter, you are referring here to the documents filed by the appellant I think on the 21st?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: 19th of January, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: 19th of January, to which you have made objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Well, the Chamber will consider that, and if it has a decision to make, it will make it in the usual way between now and the 19th of April, in good time for anybody who is interested in taking consequential measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Have I overlooked some matter which is of relevance and importance to the proceedings? I turn to my colleagues. The bench is content, the bar is content, and the proceedings are adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: 1.15 p.m., to be reconvened on Monday, the 19th day of April, 1999, at 10.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
